svg.title: Optimistic Concurrency Control
svg.desc: Optimistic Concurrency Control. Update a row only if it is unchanged since you read it, using a version column, and retry on conflict instead of holding locks. Step 1, Last write wins: Two agents read the order, then save in turn: B's UPDATE overwrites A's fix, and both get UPDATE 1. Step 2, Save only if unchanged: Each save checks AND version = $2 and bumps it: A's returns version 2, B's matches 0 rows. Step 3, If-Match over HTTP: The version travels as an ETag: B's stale If-Match gets 412, so B reloads, merges and saves again. Step 4, Limits and alternatives: Never lock through think time; a hot row makes most attempts conflict; a counter beats a timestamp.

g.text: Two agents read the order, then save in turn: B's UPDATE overwrites A's fix, and both get UPDATE 1.
Each save checks AND version = $2 and bumps it: A's returns version 2, B's matches 0 rows.
The version travels as an ETag: B's stale If-Match gets 412, so B reloads, merges and saves again.
Never lock through think time; a hot row makes most attempts conflict; a counter beats a timestamp.
WHAT TO USE AS A VERSION
WHAT EACH SESSION RAN AND SAW
PostgreSQL 18.6 · each statement commits on its own
SELECT shipping_address FROM orders WHERE id = 499996
SELECT shipping_address FROM orders WHERE id = 499996
UPDATE orders SET shipping_address = '88/5 Sukhumvit 11, Bangkok' WHERE id = 499996
UPDATE orders SET shipping_address = '88 Sukhumvit 11, Bangkok 10110' WHERE id = 499996
Each agent reads, edits for minutes, then saves. The read and the save are separate transactions,
so B’s UPDATE overwrites a row B never saw: A’s /5 is lost and nobody is told.
Run each save in a SERIALIZABLE
B read minutes earlier, in a
SAVE ONLY IF THE VERSION IS UNCHANGED
ALTER TABLE orders ADD COLUMN version integer NOT NULL DEFAULT 1
SELECT shipping_address, version FROM orders WHERE id = $1
UPDATE orders SET shipping_address = $3, version = version + 1
WHERE id = $1 AND version = $2 RETURNING version
Zero rows is not an error in SQL: the app checks the count and turns UPDATE 0 into a conflict.
the tool shows B the new row
